summary: The adult of Gligar, a silent, gliding fanged hunter and the rival's Platinum Pokémon. Gliscor watches for prey while hanging upside down from branches, and when the chance comes it swoops; its flight makes no sound, it carries prey off with its long tail, and its long fangs finish it. It is such a glider that, catching even a faint breeze properly, it could circle the globe without flapping once. Only a Gligar holding a Razor Fang, levelled up at night, becomes one, so it is never wild in a Gen I-IV game; Gligar lives on Route 45 in HeartGold.

anatomy.text: A winged animal (Gen 4 shape wings), 2.0 m and 42.5 kg, typed Ground and Flying: the Fang Scorpion Pokémon.
It has a lengthy tail it carries prey off with, and elongated fangs.
Light for its size (42.5 kg at 2.0 m against Gligar's 64.8 kg at 1.1 m): a body built for gliding.

diet.text: It observes prey while hanging inverted from branches, and swoops when the chance presents itself.
It uses its lengthy tail to carry off its prey, then its elongated fangs do the rest.
Its prey is never named. Gligar aims for the prey's face and injects poison (207.1, 207.4), so the line takes animals it can grab and carry.
Its level-1 moves are three fangs (Thunder Fang, Ice Fang, Fire Fang) and Poison Jab: a biter and a stinger in game form.

habitat.text: Trees with branches to hang from (Gliscor's own entry); its young cling to and nest on steep cliffs (207.2, 207.3).
It is never wild in any Gen I-IV game: it comes only from a Gligar holding a Razor Fang, levelled up at night. In HeartGold, Gligar lives on Route 45 (20%); SoulSilver has Skarmory in that slot.
No Gen 3 habitat is given (it is from Generation 4).

behavior.text: If it catches even a faint breeze properly, it can circle the globe without flapping once.
behavior.analogy: Albatrosses cross oceans almost without flapping by dynamic soaring on the wind.

behavior.text: Its activity pattern isn't stated; it evolves only at night, holding a Razor Fang, which in game terms ties the adult to the dark.

social.text: Nothing is said about groups or pairs.

reproduction.text: Bug egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium-slow growth. Its young nest on steep cliffs (207.3).

defense.text: Nothing in its own entries describes defence. Hyper Cutter keeps its Attack from being lowered; Sand Veil helps it dodge in a sandstorm.
Harden (Lv 9) and Sand Attack (Lv 5) are its defensive moves.

senses.text: It observes prey from a hanging perch before it swoops, so it hunts by sight; nothing more is said.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Gligar when Gligar levels up holding a Razor Fang at night, growing from 1.1 m to 2.0 m but losing 22 kg.
Read as development, the line goes from a cliff-clinging glider that hops home along the ground (207.3) to a branch-hanging glider that could ride the wind around the world: more airborne with age.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Its list is a hunter's: the three fangs and Poison Jab, Knock Off, Quick Attack, Fury Cutter, Feint Attack, Screech, Night Slash, Swords Dance, U-turn, X-Scissor and Guillotine (Lv 45). U-turn, a strike and a retreat, fits a swoop-and-away hunter.

ecology.text: An aerial ambush predator; with no wild Gliscor in any game, it has no place in a Johto or Kanto web. Its young are a predator of the highlands (Route 45, HeartGold).

humans.text: Nothing is said about Gliscor and people.

homestead.text: A silent glider that could scout the mountainside from the air.
It wants trees or a high beam to hang from.
Keep small Pokémon out of reach of its tail: it carries prey off.
The rival's Gliscor, hanging from the barn rafters upside down, watching the chickens, every visit.

niche.foraging: watches from an inverted perch, swoops silently, carries prey off with its tail and finishes it with its fangs

relationships.note: To hang from while it watches.

ecotypes.name: Sand-trap glider
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that pins prey in sand after the swoop: a trapping sand vortex and a feint to get past a guard. Fits dry, sandy slopes with little cover.
ecotypes.behavior: Lands with its prey and buries it in sand rather than carrying it off.

ecotypes.name: Poison-cross striker
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that leans on its poison: a venomous cross-cut and a critical slash, delivered fast. The line's sting, kept into adulthood. Fits wooded cliffs where prey is quick.
ecotypes.behavior: Strikes on the swoop and leaves; the prey dies later.

open_questions: Does it keep Gligar's cliff nests, or move to trees?
Could it really circle the globe on a breeze (472.2)?
Where are the wild Gliscor that would come from Route 45's Gligar?
